mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4.5% in the month preceding the forecast period is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-inflation policy periods (p > 0.10 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 2,000 since the previous month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite consistent monthly employment growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,300 in a month, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as strong consumer demand boosts corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after the trigger (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3 points over two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to weak manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous month and INDPRO current < INDPRO two months ago
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the supply shock (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.0% for three months indicate a cooling labor market, leading to a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales in millions) rises by more than 10% month-over-month, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return due to strong retail confidence and earnings momentum.

A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 (GDP) and CPIAUCSL (CPI) by at least 2% in the prior quarter is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to inflationary pressure outweighing growth benefits.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 current > GDPC1 previous quarter + 2% AND CPIAUCSL current > CPIAUCSL previous quarter + 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite the dual signal (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling CPIAUCSL (CPI) and rising FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return only if FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.5% in the prior month, indicating a shift toward restrictive policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < CPIAUCSL previous month AND FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS previous month + 0.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when trigger is met (p < 0.05).
